newsitem.title: USA: Florida '96 international trade tops $56 billion.
newsitem.headline: Florida '96 international trade tops $56 billion.

text.p: The value of goods shipped through Florida ports rose to a record $56.4 billion in 1996, an increase of 7.6 percent over 1995, a government and business development group said Friday.

Office machine parts and accessories, including computer equipment, surpassed fertilizers as the top export through Florida ports, Enterprise Florida Inc said. Exports in that category have risen 60.2 percent since 1994 and totalled $1.7 billion in 1996.
Brazil remained Florida's number one trading partner in 1996, followed by Japan, Colombia, Venezuela, the Dominican Republic, Argentina, Honduras, Germany, Costa Rica and Chile.

The Miami Customs District, which covers the southern half of the state, had a value of $41.1 billion in 1996 total trade, an increase of 10.5 percent over 1995. The Miami district's 1996 imports totalled $16.6 billion, while exports totalled $24.5 billion.

The Tampa Customs District, which covers the northern half of the state, had a 1996 trade value of $15.3 billion, an increase of 0.5 percent over 1995. Imports totalled $8.4 billion and exports totalled $6.9 billion.
Enterprise Florida is a public-private partnership that took over many duties performed by the now-defunct Florida Commerce Department.
